title: Barrett Deems in blackface and Louis's remark
summary: Trummy Young tells of Armstrong's white drummer Barrett Deems being made to wear blackface in 'High Society' and of Louis forgetting he was white.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Just in closing in this incident, Tommy Young told me a wonderful story -- a couple of wonderful stories, well, he told me a thousand wonderful stories, but the one that comes to mind is about Louis. One comes to mind -- when they made the picture, I think it was "High Society" -- if you ever remember watching Louis Armstrong's band, you'll see his drummer who looks a little strange back there, and it's Barrett Deems, and the damn producers insisted that he wear blackface, and that's a beautiful thing if you knew Barrett Deems. However, the other story that comes to mind is about Barrett Deems -- is Louis Armstrong had figured he was surrounded by blacks, and that's just the thing he took for granted, and when, of course, to the uninitiated,

Barrett Deems is white, and there was one time in the dressing room, we were sitting around drinking and everything, and Trummy was sitting there, he said Louis looked at his manager, and he said, "Do me a favor; go tell that nigger on drums to play softer behind my playing -- my singing" -- and I think that was worth a chuckle.
